questions.stem: What volume does 0.5 mol of any gas occupy at room temperature and pressure (RTP)?
questions.explanation: At RTP, 1 mole of any gas occupies 24 dm³. Therefore, 0.5 mol occupies 0.5 × 24 = 12 dm³. This applies to all gases regardless of their identity.

questions.stem: What volume of hydrogen gas is produced at RTP when 6 g of magnesium reacts with excess HCl? Mg + 2HCl → MgCl₂ + H₂ (Ar: Mg = 24)
questions.explanation: Moles of Mg = 6/24 = 0.25 mol. From the equation, the Mg:H₂ ratio is 1:1, so moles of H₂ = 0.25 mol. Volume = 0.25 × 24 = 6 dm³.
